answer: Anti-Sybil via live kernel attestations: each identity must keep a signed mini-module loaded in its runtime kernel. Auditors issue a quartz nonce; the module returns a keyed MAC over nonce plus process start time. Peers verify the MAC against the registered public key and that only one warm kernel session answers. Fake identities that wander onto a shared host collide on the single module instance, so each clone needs its own always-on runtime. Limitation: identical VM fleets still pay only linear compute, and a rooted host can spoof MACs until diversity checks flag it.
